text.p: Chief executives of Krupp and Thyssen AG have begun talks about merging their steel operations at an undisclosed location, a Thyssen spokesman said.
The talks are aimed at reaching a mutually acceptable plan within eight days, or Krupp will resume its 13.6 billion mark ($8.1 billion) hostile takeover bid for all of its larger rival Thyssen.

Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp chairman Gerhard Cromme and Thyssen chairman Dieter Vogel are heading the talks, under the mediation of Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner and former Preussag Stahl AG chairman Kurt Staehler, the Thyssen spokesman said.
He declined to give further details on the location, agenda, planned length of the session or other participants, saying the talks must be allowed to proceed undisturbed.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.686 German Marks)
